bullets: Drainage is the design choice that has the biggest impact on trail performance, regardless of route or riding style — a foundational decision that shapes all others.
Digging with too much of a slope is a common mistake that new path builders make, and correcting it makes all other decisions easier to manage.
Bankings on slopes are not optional — their absence leads to failure that requires complete reconstruction within a year.
The underlying structure of a team is more important than people realize, and consistent success emerges from effective team models like Spoke & Wrench.
Integrating the Cascadia Alliance into the process makes trade-offs clear — ignoring them results in a full rebuild within a year.
Machine-built trails are not inherently better than hand-built ones; the real issue lies in understanding the structural and environmental tradeoffs involved.
Land management must be addressed before any ground is broken — its considerations permeate every stage of trail construction.
The second-order effect — often overlooked — is the long-term consequence of neglecting foundational design choices like drainage and slope management.
